findings.issue_text: Site-configurable size limits (max_<type>_size_kb, max_image_size_kb) silently replaced with hardcoded 10MB, breaking admin-configured limits in both directions (utilities.js:182, :246, uploads_controller.rb:55)
The 413 handler (utilities.js:246) reports "10 MB" regardless of the web server's real limit, so the error message can be wrong
Per-type size settings (different limits for avatars vs. attachments) flattened to one value for all types

OptimizedImage.downsize signature change from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions_string) breaks other existing callers, with width misinterpreted and height dropped producing malformed ImageMagick instructions
The same contract change applied to resize breaks its existing callers

In-place downsize (tempfile.path to tempfile.path) can truncate/corrupt the uploaded file on failure; convert_with returns false but the loop keeps retrying against the corrupt file and Upload.create_for receives the damaged image
No check of downsize's return value and no backup of the original, so a failed convert causes data loss of the user's upload
Downsize loop retries with the same parameters up to 5 times without verifying size actually decreased, so it can spin and upload the oversized file anyway

"80%" passed as the dimensions string may not be valid for downsize_instructions which expects WxH geometry; if the generated convert flag is invalid every iteration is a silent no-op and the feature never works
For API URL uploads, filename derived from URL basename may lack an image extension, failing FileHelper.is_image? and skipping the downsize path inconsistently with direct file uploads

Non-image uploads bypass the type-specific size check client-side since max_<type>_size_kb lookup is removed, so users get the raw 413 handler instead of the friendly client-side message for attachments

CPU-heavy image re-encoding loop runs synchronously in the web request thread — P1 (confidence 75): up to 5 full ImageMagick passes per upload execute inline in the controller, blocking Puma workers and spiking memory, with no concurrency limit (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70)

Fixed 5-attempt "80%" loop may re-encode lossless formats with no size reduction — P2 (confidence 50): for PNG, downscaling by 80% may never reduce size below the limit, causing 5 full decodes/re-encodes with no benefit and no check that the previous iteration shrank the file (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-68)

Signature change to OptimizedImage.downsize breaks other callers — P0 (confidence 75): downsize changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions_string), so 4-arg callers raise ArgumentError and the removal of self.dimensions breaks remaining callers (app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-148)

Client-side hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings — P2 (confidence 75): client hardcodes 10MB for all types, diverging from server-side SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and funneling every "too large" upload into the synchronous downsize path (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182, 246)

Animated GIFs silently lose animation during downsize: `optimize` only selects the `_animated` instructions variant when `from` matches `.GIF`, but the controller passes a temp path with no extension, so animation is stripped with no error; `allow_animation:` is effectively dead code for this path

Downsize failure is silently ignored: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on imagemagick failure, the return value is discarded, and the oversized tempfile is passed to `Upload.create_for` anyway, reintroducing oversized uploads/413 with no fallback error, log, or rejection

`OptimizedImage.downsize` signature change from `(from, to, max_width, max_height)` to `(from, to, dimensions_string)` breaks existing callers still passing four arguments, raising ArgumentError at runtime and potentially breaking thumbnail generation in codebase/plugins

Hardcoded 10MB client check bypasses site settings: pre-upload check and 413 handler use hardcoded `10 * 1024` instead of SiteSettings, so admins can no longer configure upload limits and type-specific limits (e.g. avatars) are silently relaxed to 10MB client-side

Error message hardcodes 10MB while server limit is separately configurable: if `max_image_size_kb` is set to e.g. 4MB, files between 4–10MB pass the client check and may fail server-side with a misleading message claiming a 10MB limit; also the API/download path caps downloads at 10MB regardless of the configured setting

Downsize loop retries on persistent imagemagick failure with no backoff or diagnostic logging, adding latency from 5 imagemagick invocations per upload and making the eventual oversized-upload failure undiagnosable

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Site-configurable size limits (max_<type>_size_kb, max_image_size_kb) silently replaced with hardcoded 10MB, breaking admin-configured limits in both directions (utilities.js:182, :246, uploads_controller.rb:55)
The 413 handler (utilities.js:246) reports "10 MB" regardless of the web server's real limit, so the error message can be wrong

adjudication.rationale: In utilities.js the 413 (entity too large) handler was changed from using `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hard-coded `10 * 1024` with comment "10 MB". A 413 is typically enforced by the web server/reverse proxy, whose limit may differ from 10MB, so the displayed `post.errors.file_too_large` message can report the wrong maximum size. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-type size settings (different limits for avatars vs. attachments) flattened to one value for all types

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces per-type size limits with a single hardcoded 10MB cap. In `utilities.js`, `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` is replaced by `10 * 1024` for all upload `type`s, flattening different limits (e.g., avatar vs attachment). Additionally, the 413 handler and URL download limit in `uploads_controller.rb` are also hardcoded to 10MB (`10 * 1024`, `10.megabytes`) instead of using the relevant SiteSettings. This changes behavior and ignores configured per-type limits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedImage.downsize signature change from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions_string) breaks other existing callers, with width misinterpreted and height dropped producing malformed ImageMagick instructions

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, `downsize` is defined twice: first as `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`, then later redefined as `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition overrides the earlier one, so any existing callers still using the old arity (e.g., passing width/height separately, or passing 5 args including opts) would now raise `ArgumentError` or mis-bind arguments (height becoming `opts`), leading to invalid instruction generation. This is a real behavioral/API break introduced by the diff, even though only one new call site is shown updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The same contract change applied to resize breaks its existing callers

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OptimizedImage.resize(from, to, width, height, opts={})` keeps the same public signature (still takes `width, height`). Only the internal call to `optimize` changes to pass a preformatted dimensions string. While `optimize`’s signature changes, `resize` is updated accordingly, so existing `resize` callers are not shown to break by this diff. (Separately, `downsize` is redefined later with a different arity, but that is not what the finding claims.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: In-place downsize (tempfile.path to tempfile.path) can truncate/corrupt the uploaded file on failure; convert_with returns false but the loop keeps retrying against the corrupt file and Upload.create_for receives the damaged image

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an in-place image rewrite: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in `uploads_controller.rb`. `OptimizedImage.optimize` ultimately calls `convert_with(...)`, which returns `false` on nonzero exit status, but the controller loop ignores the return value and continues decrementing attempts and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` regardless. While the diff doesn’t prove that ImageMagick will truncate/corrupt the file when `from == to`, the in-place write combined with ignored failure handling is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness issue that could result in uploading a bad/partially processed file if conversion fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check of downsize's return value and no backup of the original, so a failed convert causes data loss of the user's upload

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new auto-downsize loop runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place (same `from` and `to`) and ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on conversion failure, but the controller does not check it or keep a copy of the original tempfile before overwriting. If the convert operation fails or partially writes when input==output, the original upload content could be corrupted and still passed to `Upload.create_for`, causing potential data loss of the user’s upload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop retries with the same parameters up to 5 times without verifying size actually decreased, so it can spin and upload the oversized file anyway

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop attempts up to 5 downsizes while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but after the loop it proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without any explicit check that the final `tempfile.size` is now within the limit. If `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` fails to reduce the file (same parameters each time) the loop just exhausts attempts and continues. The finding’s claim that it can still proceed with an oversized file is grounded in this diff, though whether it ultimately gets rejected depends on validations not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: "80%" passed as the dimensions string may not be valid for downsize_instructions which expects WxH geometry; if the generated convert flag is invalid every iteration is a silent no-op and the feature never works
matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that passing "80%" as the resize dimensions is incompatible with a path that expects WxH geometry, leading to a silent failure/no-op. The golden comment is specific to the animated GIF path using gifsicle --resize-fit, while the candidate describes the same underlying geometry-mismatch problem more generally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For API URL uploads, filename derived from URL basename may lack an image extension, failing FileHelper.is_image? and skipping the downsize path inconsistently with direct file uploads

adjudication.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsize block is gated by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`. For API URL uploads, `filename` is set via `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`, which can plausibly be empty or lack an extension (e.g. URLs with no path or with query-based filenames). In that case the image may not be recognized as an image by `is_image?`, so the newly added downsizing logic would be skipped for URL uploads while it would run for direct uploads using `file.original_filename`. This is a diff-grounded edge case affecting the intended new behavior, though whether it manifests depends on how `is_image?` works and typical URL formats.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-image uploads bypass the type-specific size check client-side since max_<type>_size_kb lookup is removed, so users get the raw 413 handler instead of the friendly client-side message for attachments

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the type-specific `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` lookup and replaces it with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` check, but non-image uploads do not “bypass” client-side size checking—they are still checked against 10MB and will still get the same `bootbox.alert` message if exceeded. Also, the 413 handler is not “raw”: it explicitly shows the same `post.errors.file_too_large` alert (now also hardcoded to 10MB). The claim about users getting a raw 413 instead of a friendly message isn’t supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CPU-heavy image re-encoding loop runs synchronously in the web request thread — P1 (confidence 75): up to 5 full ImageMagick passes per upload execute inline in the controller, blocking Puma workers and spiking memory, with no concurrency limit (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63-70)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous re-encoding/downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload`: up to 5 iterations calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` (new block around lines 60-70). `OptimizedImage` ultimately runs ImageMagick via backticks in `convert_with`, so this work executes inline during the web request, potentially consuming CPU/memory and blocking Puma workers. This is a performance/architecture concern created by the change rather than a direct functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fixed 5-attempt "80%" loop may re-encode lossless formats with no size reduction — P2 (confidence 50): for PNG, downscaling by 80% may never reduce size below the limit, causing 5 full decodes/re-encodes with no benefit and no check that the previous iteration shrank the file (app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66-68)

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side loop (uploads_controller.rb) repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while `tempfile.size` remains above the limit, but it does not track whether the previous iteration actually reduced the file size (or otherwise made progress). From the diff alone, this creates a plausible inefficiency/extra re-encode risk for some image types where re-encoding may not shrink as expected, though it’s not a clearly verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Signature change to OptimizedImage.downsize breaks other callers — P0 (confidence 75): downsize changed from (from, to, max_width, max_height) to (from, to, dimensions_string), so 4-arg callers raise ArgumentError and the removal of self.dimensions breaks remaining callers (app/models/optimized_image.rb:146-148)

Client-side hardcoded 10MB limit ignores site settings — P2 (confidence 75): client hardcodes 10MB for all types, diverging from server-side SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and funneling every "too large" upload into the synchronous downsize path (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182, 246)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the client-side max size derived from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` and `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` with a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js` (both the pre-upload check and the 413 handler). This verifiably ignores site-configured limits and can cause the client to accept uploads that the server may still reject or handle differently (server still uses `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` and only downsizes images in `UploadsController`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Animated GIFs silently lose animation during downsize: `optimize` only selects the `_animated` instructions variant when `from` matches `.GIF`, but the controller passes a temp path with no extension, so animation is stripped with no error; `allow_animation:` is effectively dead code for this path

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated-path selection is gated by `from =~ /\.GIF$/i` plus `opts[:allow_animation]`. The controller’s new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`, where `tempfile.path` is typically a temp file without the original `.gif` extension. As a result, even for an uploaded animated GIF (identified via `filename`), the `_animated` instructions variant will not be used during this downsizing step, plausibly stripping animation without warning and making `allow_animation:` ineffective for this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize failure is silently ignored: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false on imagemagick failure, the return value is discarded, and the oversized tempfile is passed to `Upload.create_for` anyway, reintroducing oversized uploads/413 with no fallback error, log, or rejection

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value and never verifies that `tempfile.size` is <= `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after the attempts. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on imagemagick failure, so a downsize failure can leave the tempfile unchanged/oversized and the code still proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` with the oversized file. The finding’s core claim (failure is ignored and oversized file can still be uploaded/processed) is supported by the diff, even if the exact downstream symptom (413) depends on code not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Error message hardcodes 10MB while server limit is separately configurable: if `max_image_size_kb` is set to e.g. 4MB, files between 4–10MB pass the client check and may fail server-side with a misleading message claiming a 10MB limit; also the API/download path caps downloads at 10MB regardless of the configured setting

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly hardcodes upload limits/messages to 10MB in the client (`maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` in `utilities.js`, including the 413 error path) instead of using `Discourse.SiteSettings[...]`, so the UI/validation no longer reflects the configurable server setting. It also hardcodes the API URL download cap to `10.megabytes` in `uploads_controller.rb` instead of `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, so downloads are capped independently of configuration. These are real behavioral changes shown in the diff and can cause misleading limits and mismatches with configured settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Downsize loop retries on persistent imagemagick failure with no backoff or diagnostic logging, adding latency from 5 imagemagick invocations per upload and making the eventual oversized-upload failure undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop retries up to 5 times purely while `tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` each time, but it does not check whether `OptimizedImage.downsize` succeeded (and `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` on failure without raising/logging). If ImageMagick persistently fails, the file size likely won’t change and the loop will still incur up to 5 invocations with no backoff and no diagnostic logging, matching the finding’s latency/undiagnosability concern. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/observability issue rather than a clear functional defect proven by the diff alone.
